content:
dave: Heads up — since ~08:10 UTC multiple GPU nodes in us-west2 are flipping to NotReady + NoSchedule. Lots of gpu pods pending. Anyone oncall?

carla: I'm on it. Can you paste `kubectl get nodes` + daemonset status?

dave: Sure — clipped output: 
```
> kubectl get nodes -o wide | egrep 'gpu|ready'
NODE1   NotReady   <none>   20d   10.1.2.3   us-west2   cos-123
NODE2   NotReady   <none>   18d   10.1.2.4   us-west2   cos-123
NODE3   Ready      <none>   2d    10.1.2.5   us-west2   cos-123
```
DaemonSet: `nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset` shows 3 desired, 0 available, pods CrashLoopBackOff.

carla: Ok — looks like the device-plugin container cannot talk to the driver. Can you grab logs: `kubectl -n kube-system logs ds/nvidia-device-plugin -c nvidia-device-plugin`

dave: Logs show: 
```
E0418 08:12:03.123456   1 plugin.go:120] plugin registration failed: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection closed
2026/04/18 08:12:04 nvidia-smi failed: exit status 1
NVIDIA-SMI has failed because it couldn't communicate with the NVIDIA driver. Make sure the latest NVIDIA driver is installed and running.
```

brian: That error + cos image suggests the node kernel/driver didn't load after a kernel update or driver kubelet module mismatch. Happens if the underlying image bumped kernel and DKMS didn't rebuild. Were there any infra updates rolled last night?

dave: We had a node-pool rolling update at 03:00am UTC (auto image patch). Not sure if GPU driver daemonset ran successfully after the reboot.

alice: Quick triage: device plugin requires the kernel module. If `nvidia-smi` fails on the node, the Kubelet will mark GPU resources unavailable and the plugin will crash. Steps:
- SSH one affected node and run `sudo nvidia-smi` and `dmesg | grep NVRM`
- Try `sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced` or reinstall driver via the node-level installer/daemonset.

carla: Before we reimage anything, try restarting the plugin DS: `kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart ds/nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset` and check `kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l name=nvidia-device-plugin -o wide`

dave: Did rollout restart — pods come up then immediately log same driver error. `nvidia-smi` on node returns: 
```
NVRM: The NVIDIA GPU driver is not loaded
```
So restarting plugin doesn't help because driver isn't loaded at kernel level.

brian: This explains CA behavior — cluster-autoscaler keeps scaling because pending pods request `nvidia.com/gpu`. New nodes join but their GPUs are unusable, so they remain effectively unschedulable. CA keeps re-adding capacity -> risk of cost spike. We should temporarily pause CA scaling on the affected nodepool(s).

alice: Agreed. Immediate mitigations: 
- `kubectl cordon` affected nodes to stop scheduling new pods there.
- Pause cluster-autoscaler for that pool (or set `maxnodes=0` temporary) so we don't spin up more broken nodes.
- Create a replacement node pool with the known-good GPU image (cos-gpu-driver-vX.Y) and migrate workloads.

carla: For faster fix: if kernel module missing, sometimes a reboot fixes DKMS rebuild. But GKE COS may not have DKMS enabled. Safer path: reprovision nodepool with the GPU-enabled image.

dave: I'll cordon the two NotReady nodes and pause CA. Then I'll create a new nodepool `gpu-pool-usw2-v2` with image `cos-2026-gpu-1.2.3` and allow 0->2 nodes, test there.

alice: Also add this to runbook: check `kubectl describe node <node>` -> look for `Taints` and `Allocatable` showing `nvidia.com/gpu: 0` when driver missing. Example: 
```
Allocatable:
  cpu:  8
  memory: 30Gi
  nvidia.com/gpu: 0
Taints:
  nvidia.com/gpu:NoSchedule
```
If allocatable GPU is zero while hardware exists, driver is not registered.

brian: After we reprovision, we should update autoscaler config to tolerate short NotReady windows (scale-up delay) and add a health-check hook: mark node as unschedulable for CA until driver plugin reports available. Otherwise CA will treat nodes as ready and still fail scheduling.

infra-bot: Incident INC-5124 created: "us-west2 GPU driver failure -> NotReady nodes". PagerDuty alerted ops-oncall. Ticket #1229 linked.

dave: Action plan executed: cordoned nodes, CA paused for pool, new nodepool created. I'll monitor for 30m and then start migrating test jobs. Will update in this thread. :thumbsup:
